newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee strengthens on dollar, pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee strengthens on dollar, pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee strengthened against both the dollar and pound on Friday, reflecting the weakening of the U.S. currency in overnight international markets, forex dealers said.
The rupee was fixed at a mean commercial rate of 20.018 against the dollar from 20.051 on Thursday. It was quoted at a mean rate of 32.2595 to a pound from 32.5980 on Thursday.
Forex dealers said the rupee's fixing on Friday was in line with the weaker dollar in international markets.
"On the local front, a couple of commercial banks are long in their foreign exchange positions owing to the lower than average demand from importers.
"They (importers) are not rushing in to make their payments before their bills fall due," one dealer said. He expected importers' bills to fall due by January-end to early February.
On the week, the rupee strengthened against the dollar from a mean rate of 20.061 last Friday.
The central bank was seen supporting the rupee during market interventions on Monday and Tuesday.
"The central bank sold dollars at the prevailing interbank bid rates during the interventions and this supported the rupee by providing liquidity in the market," the dealer said.
